title: Incident Context Strip: Quick Handoffs, Cost Flags, and Postmortem Anchors
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
Design a compact, single-line 'Incident Context Strip' to sit at the top of an Alert/Incident detail panel that surfaces critical context and fast handoff actions without overwhelming the on-call. The strip combines a minimal SLO snapshot, a cost-impact flag, on-call quick actions, and an anchor to postmortem/runbook resources. Goal is to reduce mean time-to-handoff and make post-incident follow-up discoverable from the moment an alert is opened.

Problem & user needs:
- On-call engineers and incident commanders need one-click access to: current SLO health, whether this alert is likely to cause billing spikes (cost flag), the person/team owning the next shift, and a direct link to postmortem templates or runbooks.
- Current alert detail requires navigation across tabs and panels; handoffs are slow and postmortems are often created after context is lost.

Design concept (high level):
- Compact strip (40–48px height) with 5 micro-areas: 1) SLO chip + sparkline, 2) Burn-rate indicator, 3) Cost-impact badge (low/medium/high with estimated hourly token cost), 4) On-call pill (name + role, click to page or escalate), 5) Postmortem anchor + runbook preview (hover/expand).
- Default collapsed state shows SLO chip (green/amber/red), cost badge, and on-call pill. Expanding (keyboard + click) reveals a lightweight runbook preview and 'Create postmortem' CTA.
- Accessibility: semantic elements, ARIA labels for each micro-area, keyboard-expandable, color contrast meets AA.

Trade-offs & decisions made:
- Compact vs. detailed: Chose compact strip to minimize vertical space and focus on primary decisions. Deeper timeline or full SLO trend moved to the Alerts timeline tab to avoid duplication.
- Cost estimate: Provide a coarse estimated token-hour cost bucket instead of exact numbers to avoid noise and billing discussions in high-pressure incidents. Engineers can click through to the cost dashboard for precise numbers.
- Privacy: Avoid showing customer-identifying strings in the on-call context; show team alias and hashed org id when needed.
- Performance: The strip must load with low priority data so initial alert open is instant. SLO and cost values fetched via a single bundled endpoint (ENG dependency) and cached per alert. If data unavailable, the strip shows skeletons and a 'retry' affordance.

Prototype & artifacts:
- Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/REDWOOD/incident-context-strip-prototype (prototype frames + interaction notes)
- PRD: https://docs.internal.redwood.com/console/alerts/incident-context-strip-prd
- Clickable prototype (InVision): https://invision.redwood.com/preview/ICS-2025
- Dev spike ticket: ENG-21234 (API bundling endpoint for strip data)

User testing (summary):
- N=6 participants (SREs / on-call engineers). Tasks: find SLO status, initiate handoff, start postmortem. Success rates: find SLO 100%, initiate handoff 83% (first-click confusion for 'page' vs 'assign'), start postmortem 100% via anchor. Key feedback: emphasize affordance for paging; reduce visual similarity between cost badge and alert severity.

Acceptance criteria (must be met for design sign-off):
- Visual spec for collapsed and expanded states (desktop + tablet + mobile) in Figma.
- Interaction spec: keyboard expansion, ARIA labels, hover/press states.
- List of API fields required from ENG (SLO status, 7-day sparkline miniature, burn rate, cost bucket, current on-call alias, runbook link, postmortem template link).
- Responsive fallback: mobile shows single-row stacked wrap with a single 'More' overflow menu.
- Security/RBAC: postmortem anchor respects access rules; for users without permission show 'Request access' CTA.

Open questions & proposed follow-ups:
- Do we surface exact estimated cost numbers in the initial design or keep to buckets? (PM leaning: buckets)
- How should the strip behave for alerts mapped to multiple services/teams? (Proposed: show primary owner and a 'multiple' indicator that opens owner list.)
- Confirm telemetry events with analytics team to track "used handoff action" and "created postmortem from strip" for ROI measurement.

Next steps:
- Iterate on micro-interaction for 'page' CTA to disambiguate from 'assign' (Design: Aiden).
- Finalize API contract with ENG-21234 and ENG-21300 (blocked until API schema confirmed).
- Run a broader usability test (N=12) including incident commanders and first responders.
- Prepare design handoff package (tokens, spacing, accessible spec) and schedule dev sync 2025-03-07.

Related tickets and assets:
- Parent: PM-4412 (Alerts UX initiative)
- Dev: ENG-21234 (strip API), ENG-21300 (on-call paging integration)
- QA checklist: QA-901 (accessibility), QA-902 (responsive behavior)
